subject: ISV compatibility dashboard RFC & integration data request
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@matrixtools.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring a compatibility dashboard between Matrix Tools and Redwood

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the quick intro from Marissa last week. Matrix Tools builds observability and integration tooling for ISVs and system integrators; our partners keep asking for a single-pane view that shows which SDKs / runtimes and ecosystem tooling are supported by a given LLM inference provider.

We would love to collaborate on a lightweight "compatibility dashboard" that maps Redwood capabilities to common ISV integration points (LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, tracing hooks, prompt-tool connectors, caching/KV affinity, quantization profiles). High-level asks from our side:

- A short API/schema spec for your SDKs (current versions and supported features)
- Tracing hook semantics (span names, OTLP endpoints, sampling semantics)
- Any existing compatibility matrices that show supported operations (e.g., streaming, function-calls, tokenization hooks)

If this is something Redwood would be open to co-publishing, we can draft a partner page and prototype dashboard tiles. Happy to sign an NDA if needed — but to start, could you share a contact and a short list of data we can programmatically pull?

Thanks and talk soon,
Elena Torres
Head of Integrations | Matrix Tools
attachments: matrix-sample-integration-map.png (image stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@matrixtools.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a compatibility dashboard between Matrix Tools and Redwood

Elena —

Really interested in this idea. Redwood is actively working to make ISV integrations first-class, and a compatibility dashboard would help ISVs and customers choose the right workflows. I attached a short draft RFC (redwood-isv-compat-rfc-v1.pdf) that outlines our proposed data model and the fields we can expose. Quick notes:

- We can export a JSON compatibility manifest per model+runtime with fields like supported_adapter_flags (langchain, llamalndex, llm_streaming, function_calling), recommended_quant_profile, observed_latency_p50_ms (sampled), token_cost_per_1k, and tracing_support (OTLP: yes/no, span_map reference).
- Privacy: manifests would not include customer-specific data. For runtime telemetry we can provide aggregated, sampled numbers or a synthetic microbenchmark set.
- Timeline: we can produce a v1 manifest for our curated models in ~2 weeks if we align on the data contract.

Next steps I propose:
1) Matrix sends a short template of the dashboard tiles you plan to show (we can map directly).
2) We finalize the JSON schema (see attached RFC).
3) Kickoff a 30-min technical sync next week to go through tracing and SDK hooks.

Cc'ing Marissa to own the compatibility table and Karthik for tracing/telemetry details.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-isv-compat-rfc-v1.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@matrixtools.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a compatibility dashboard between Matrix Tools and Redwood

Thanks Vivek — I'll take the lead on the compatibility table. A couple of product asks to make this practical for customers and partners:

- Use a three-state support label per feature: Full | Partial | Planned (helps set expectations).
- For features that affect economics/perf include small benchmark columns: p50 latency delta (ms) vs base, token-cost delta (%), and guidance on best-practice runtime configs (batch size, KV cache on/off).
- Add a "Notes" free-text column for known limitations (e.g., "streaming not supported for quantized int4 models") and a link to a short runbook.

I've started a working sheet — https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ExampleSheet — feel free to add sample rows. I'll also populate initial rows for LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters with our current support matrix.

Marissa
Sr. Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@matrixtools.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a compatibility dashboard between Matrix Tools and Redwood

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 11:05 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Tracing_support (OTLP: yes/no, span_map reference)

Quick technical notes from the runtime side:

- We support OTLP ingestion for spans. For the dashboard, the minimal contract is: OTLP boolean, default_sampling_rate (if any), and a stable set of span names and attributes.
- Proposed span naming convention: redwood.request.start, redwood.request.tokenize, redwood.request.kvcache.hit, redwood.request.kvcache.miss, redwood.request.end. Mapping these to LangChain/LlamaIndex events is straightforward but we'll need adapter-level instrumentation guidance (examples in the RFC appendix).
- Caveat on sampling: high-volume customers often have sampling windows; we can surface the configured sampling rate but not the raw traces.

I'll paste a short example mapping for LangChain:
- LangChain: LLMChain.call -> maps to redwood.request.start / .end
- LlamaIndex: QueryEngine.query -> maps to redwood.request.start / .tokenize / .end

If Matrix intends to show trace-level correlation in the dashboard, we'll need a signed data-sharing addendum. Otherwise aggregate counts + boolean tracing support should be enough for v1.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@matrixtools.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring a compatibility dashboard between Matrix Tools and Redwood

Vivek / Marissa / Karthik —

This is great, thank you. We reviewed the RFC and the mapping suggestions and agree on a v1 scope:

- Expose a per-model JSON manifest with feature flags (Full/Partial/Planned), p50 sample latency, token-cost estimate, quantization recommendations, and a small tracing_support object (OTLP: true/false + span_list reference).
- Matrix will build a prototype dashboard showing tiles for LangChain, LlamaIndex, and a generic "prompt-tools" connector. We'll wire the tiles to the sample manifests and share a draft by next Friday.

Action items:
- Redwood: finalize JSON schema and drop the redwood-isv-compat-rfc-v1.pdf into the shared doc (Vivek / Marissa) — due Tue 16 Mar.
- Matrix: prototype tiles and sample data — due Fri 19 Mar.
- Both: 30-min technical sync scheduled Thu, 18 Mar at 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite to follow).

Attachments: matrix-sample-integration-map.png, redwood-isv-compat-rfc-v1.pdf

Elena Torres
Head of Integrations | Matrix Tools
